sentences.text:
This Petition Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioner-accused N9o.1, who is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 419, 420, 463, 468, 468, 471 R/w Section 34 of IPC, filed an application under Section 457 of Cr.P.C. before the learned Magistrate to release the vehicle bearing No.KA-28/Z-7613 of Maruti Suzuki Ertiga Samart HYBRID ZXI+ motor cab and the said vehicle was seized from the custody of accused No.1, who is the registered owner of the said vehicle.

entities.text: Maruti Suzuki Ertiga Samart HYBRID ZXI+ motor cab
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The learned Magistrate, by order dated 17.01.2022, dismissed the said application, against which, a revision petition was filed.
The learned District Judge dismissed the revision petition.
Hence, this petition.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent- State.
3. The petitioner, to prove that he is the owner of the vehicle has produced the notarized copy of Registration Certificate, Insurance Policy and Aadhar Card.

However, the learned Magistrate and the learned Sessions Judge have dismissed the application stating that the petitioner has not NC:
2023:KHC-K:5615 produced the source of income for having purchased the said vehicle.

4. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sunderbhai Ambalal Desai vs. State of Gujarat reported in (2002) 10 SCC 283 has held that, it is of no use to keep such seized vehicles at the police stations for a long period.

entities.text: Sunderbhai Ambalal Desai vs. State of Gujarat reported in (2002) 10 SCC 283
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is for the Magistrate to pass appropriate orders immediately by taking appropriate bond and guarantee as well as security for return of the said vehicles, if required at any point of time.
5. Since the Registration Certificate indicates that the said vehicle belongs to petitioner-accused No.1, he is entitled for release of the same by imposing suitable conditions.

Accordingly, I pass the Sardar Nayak vs The State on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62745348/
2 following:
ORDER Criminal Petition is allowed.
